## Contribute component-performance evidence

You do not need Rust, CMake, or a microphone to contribute a component benchmark. From a clean Syllabix checkout, run:

```bash
./scripts/contribute-performance.sh
```

The script uses an in-tree release binary or `syllabix` on your `PATH`; otherwise it downloads and checksum-verifies the matching GitHub Release. It fills the cache for every supported local STT, LLM, and TTS id (one axis at a time — no STT×LLM×TTS cross-product), runs the isolated fixtures for each, and writes one immutable `docs/eval/runs/<fingerprint>.jsonl` submission. The fingerprint includes OS/arch/CPU/cores/RAM plus the ggml compute backend (`cpu` / `metal` / `vulkan`) and, when known, GPU name and VRAM — so a CPU run and a Vulkan run on the same host do not collide. It does not run the voice loop, open a device, measure AEC or barge-in, or make a live-latency claim.

If `gh` is authenticated, the script creates a branch, commits only that JSONL file, and opens a PR. Without it, the JSONL remains in place and the script prints the exact commands to finish. Developers changing the harness can instead use the explicit toolchain fallback:

```bash
./scripts/contribute-performance.sh --from-source
```

If a previous run preserved an uncommitted JSONL for the same fingerprint, a later invocation validates and reuses that record; a fingerprint already committed to Git remains immutable and is rejected.

`docs/workload_benchmark/*.csv` (one statistics file per model, rows split by machine) and `docs/workload_benchmark/workload_benchmark.md` (tables split by machine configuration) are generated locally via `python3 scripts/summarize-benchmarks.py` after a run lands; no CI publishes them. Do not hand-edit those files — re-run the script. A failed correctness verdict is still valid evidence and stays in its JSONL record.

`scripts/make-stt-manifest.py` builds a local 16 kHz WAV+TSV corpus for `syllabix bench-asr-worker --manifest`. Mix noise with `--noise` / `--snr`. `scripts/stt-bench-report.py` prints WER and latency across JSONL files for one machine fingerprint.

## VAD endpointing lab

`syllabix vad-lab` is a hidden, contributor-only command that checks whether the turn detector (Silero VAD) splits two spoken clips correctly. It joins two speech fixtures with a pause, mixes noise at a target signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), and counts the turns the detector closes across a grid of noise and pause lengths. It prints accuracy (`ok / total`) plus two failure counts — `false_split` (a turn closes too early) and `missed` (a pause swallows a turn) — and an energy probe for the echo canceller (AEC) and noise suppression (NS) stages.

```bash
cargo run -p syllabix -- vad-lab
```

It takes no arguments, uses the cached Silero model like `run` does, embeds its own fixtures, and makes no live-device claim. The frame-stepped replica of the production turn policy (threshold, min-speech latch, closing hysteresis, and the idle recurrent-state reset) is checked against the real VAD before the grid runs; any mismatch is printed. `end_silence_ms` dominates the result; the AEC and NS columns are capture-only (no render reference) and are indicative only.

## Live devices

From this checkout, `cargo run -p syllabix -- run` talks on a machine with a microphone and speakers.

```bash
cargo run -p syllabix -- run
cargo test -p syllabix-core --test audio_io hardware_record_and_play_if_devices_exist -- --ignored --nocapture
```

The echo gate needs a quiet laptop with its built-in microphone and speakers selected. Do not wear headphones or speak during this command. It allows 10 seconds for automatic calibration, then plays the versioned speech fixture continuously for 1 minute and requires Silero to detect zero false user turns:

```bash
cargo test -p syllabix-core --test audio_io hardware_aec_1_minute_playback_has_zero_false_turns -- --ignored --exact --nocapture
```

The microphone remains open throughout. Muting capture during playback does not pass. Debug dumps: `$SYLLABIX_AEC_DEBUG_DIR` or `target/aec-debug`.

To dump a live conversation, enable diagnostics in `syllabix.yaml` and run a release binary — see [diagnostics.md](diagnostics.md):

```yaml
diagnostics:
  timestamps: true
  audio: true
  directory: target/turn-debug
```

```bash
cargo run -p syllabix --release -- run
python3 scripts/summarize-timelines.py target/turn-debug
```

## Tool-harness admission (manual)

`--test harness-quality` splits **sandbox** checks from **model-quality** checks.

**Gated (must pass):** `harness_sandbox_admission` runs the four sandbox fixtures
in normal CI. A mock model emits one scripted tool call through the real executor
(`execute_with_permissions`, not `FakeSandbox`). Under Linux, `network-denied` and
`secret-denied` spawn through bubblewrap; `write-denied` is deny-before-spawn
(widening `workspace-write` on a read-only session); `cancelled-command` returns
at the shutdown check before spawn. No LLM and no API key are required; the test
asserts every sandbox fixture completes.

**Informational (0.90 bar not enforced by the combined driver):**
`harness_quality_admission` runs sandbox admission plus model-quality fixtures for
each selected agent+model pair and prints `pair=… completion=… ratio=…` lines.
Quality scoring allows careful refusals and spoken URLs; it does not re-test
sandbox policy. The combined test always exits successfully even when a pair is
below 0.90 (for example `pair=goose-local completion=0/4`). Use the legacy entry
points below when you need a hard gate on one pair. The PR evidence workflow only
requires a `pair=` line (or `skipped, no key`) per pair you ran, not a passing ratio.

**Gated at 0.90 on a single pair:** `harness_quality_live_admission` (syllabix +
online), `harness_quality_live_admission_goose` (goose + online yaml),
`harness_quality_local_lfm`, and `harness_quality_local_lfm3` assert the bar.

```bash
# Sandbox only (CI path)
cargo test -p syllabix-core --test harness-quality harness_sandbox_admission -- --nocapture

# Sandbox + all four pairs (online pairs print `skipped, no key` without SYLLABIX_LLM_API_KEY)
cargo test -p syllabix-core --test harness-quality harness_quality_admission -- --ignored --nocapture

# Offline pairs only (syllabix-local + goose-local; no API key)
SYLLABIX_HARNESS_PAIRS=offline \
  cargo test -p syllabix-core --test harness-quality harness_quality_admission -- --ignored --nocapture

# Subset of pairs (comma-separated ids: syllabix-local, syllabix-online, goose-local, goose-online)
SYLLABIX_HARNESS_PAIRS=syllabix-local,syllabix-online \
  cargo test -p syllabix-core --test harness-quality harness_quality_admission -- --ignored --nocapture
```

Online pairs need `SYLLABIX_LLM_API_KEY`, `SYLLABIX_HARNESS_BASE_URL`, and
`SYLLABIX_HARNESS_MODEL` (nothing defaulted). Local pairs need the pinned GGUF
already in the model cache; evaluation never silently downloads weights.

Model-quality fixture `current-date` checks realtime facts.
`current-date` accepts the run machine's local calendar day plus one day
before or after (timezone and midnight edges) in the spoken reply; a tool
call is optional (strong models may already know the date).

Host `web_fetch` / `web_search` use bounded public HTTP (15s read deadline per
page) — not the model-cache `BlockedFetcher`.

The built-in agent harness is on by default (`agent_harness.agent: syllabix`);
set `agent: none` for plain voice chat with no sandboxed tools. Goose local
(`goose-local`) uses Goose's own llama.cpp stack, not Syllabix's vendored LFM3
build; a low score there is a known Goose×local-LFM seam, not a missing cache file.

If your PR touches the harness boundary (`crates/syllabix-core/src/executor.rs`,
`src/openai.rs`, `src/types.rs`, `src/providers.rs`, `src/policy.rs`,
`src/sandbox/`, or `tests/harness-quality.rs`), paste the admission report into
the PR body inside an HTML comment starting with `<!-- syllabix-harness-quality
-->`, including the four sandbox fixture lines, the `sandbox summary:` line, and
a `pair=` line for each agent+model pair you ran (or `skipped, no key` for online
pairs without a key). A CI check enforces this; CI itself never calls the model.
Import-only edits on those files do not need a pasted report.

## Packaging (maintainers)

Five packages share one version: the library other apps use
(`syllabix-core`), the speech crates (`syllabix-stt`, `syllabix-tts`), the
on-device speech build they compile (`syllabix-native`), and the `syllabix`
command. Push a tag named `vX.Y.Z`. The version comes
from the tag; don't bump Cargo.toml by hand. That tag is the GitHub Release
and the crates.io publish of the four library crates. App
binaries from the GitHub Release report the same version (`./syllabix --version`).
Other apps normally depend with `syllabix-core = "0.1"`; a git pin (`tag = "vX.Y.Z"`,
or unreleased `main`) is optional. Release notes are on the tag and the
GitHub Release. If you are embedding Syllabix in another app, see
[`embed.md`](embed.md).

Pushing the tag also publishes crates to crates.io. A pull request never
uploads anything. The publish job writes the tag version (`0.1.0` for
`v0.1.0`) into Cargo.toml for that run only; it is not committed. Publish
in this order:

1. `syllabix-native` first. It contains the whisper.cpp / llama.cpp source
   the library needs to compile.
2. Then `syllabix-stt` and `syllabix-tts`, which depend on that same
   version of `syllabix-native`.
3. Then `syllabix-core`, which depends on all three.

The job waits for each version to be listed on crates.io before the next
step, and skips a crate whose version is already there.

The `syllabix` command is not on crates.io. People download the app from
GitHub Releases. The crates.io job is `.github/workflows/crates-io.yml`.
Before pushing a tag, you can rehearse it from the Actions tab (crates.io
workflow, Run workflow, enter the tag); nothing is uploaded.

Create a GitHub Release by pushing the tag only. Do not click "Create a
new release" on the GitHub Releases page. If you publish that empty
release, GitHub locks the name and this workflow cannot attach the
binaries. A leftover draft is fine: the workflow will upload onto it.
This repo uses immutable releases. Once a version's tag name has been
used for a published release, GitHub never lets that name come back, even
if you delete the release.

If that already happened, recover from the Actions tab: open the Release
workflow, Run workflow, pick the existing tag as the branch/tag, and fill
`release_name` with a name that does not start with `v` (for example
`app-v0.1.1`). The job builds from that tag and publishes the binaries
under the new name at the same commit. Leave `release_name` empty to
package artifacts without publishing.

GitHub Release files are the four artifact names plus `SHA256SUMS`. `.github/workflows/release.yml` publishes them on `v*` tags. Pull requests do not package dist binaries. If Actions cannot run, build each target with `scripts/package-release.sh` and attach with `scripts/publish-release.sh v0.1.0`.

```bash
./scripts/package-release.sh                         # host triple
./scripts/package-release.sh x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
./scripts/check-clean-artifact.sh dist/syllabix-Linux-x86_64
./scripts/smoke-offline-setup.sh dist/syllabix-Linux-x86_64
./scripts/check-repro.sh
./scripts/publish-release.sh v0.1.0
```

`cargo build -p syllabix --profile dist` is thin-LTO, one codegen unit, debuginfo stripped. Default `release` is unchanged for `ci-local.sh`.

After a Release is published, validate the documented download path: `SMOKE_RELEASE_URL=https://github.com/syllabix-ai/syllabix/releases/download/<tag> scripts/smoke-setup.sh syllabix-Linux-x86_64` (repeat per OS you can touch). The release workflow also opens a PR syncing the `vX.Y.Z` pins in the install docs (`scripts/sync-release-pins.sh`); merge it after the release.

Linux contributors who hit a missing ALSA link need `libasound2-dev`.

## Supported library API

`syllabix-core` crate-root re-exports are the Lane 2 and Lane 3 lists in
[`embed.md`](embed.md). Other public items live in named modules and can
change without notice.

Do not add a new crate-root `pub use` unless you also document it in
`docs/embed.md` (either as supported, or as explicitly not frozen). The same
rule sits above the re-exports in `crates/syllabix-core/src/lib.rs`.
`crates/syllabix-core/tests/supported_api.rs` fails if a freeze-list name
leaves the crate root, and if a crate-root re-export is missing from those
lists. The test honors `#[cfg(feature)]` so names that need `full` are
only required when those features are on.

## CI

Per-PR CI (`ci.yml`) runs on GitHub-hosted Linux: fmt, clippy, and llvm-cov
≥85% workspace lines and ≥85% lines in every reported `src/**/*.rs` file,
without loading native weights. A **native inference** check
(`native-tests.yml`) runs the real `whisper-small`, `lfm2.5-230m`,
and `pocket-tts` weights on pull requests and pushes to `main` on
`ubuntu-latest`. It runs when crates, lockfiles, setup scripts, or that
workflow change; docs-only PRs skip the heavy steps so the check still
reports. Model weights are cached with `actions/cache`, keyed on those
ids plus a hash of `manifest.rs`.
A **native serve** job in the same workflow (Linux only) starts
[`syllabix serve tts`](cli.md#serve) then `serve stt`, waits for each
`GET /health`, and runs the six-turn real loop test against those
servers (`SYLLABIX_STT_BASE_URL` / `SYLLABIX_TTS_BASE_URL`, keys
`SYLLABIX_STT_API_KEY` / `SYLLABIX_TTS_API_KEY`). Same path gate and
model cache; VAD and the LLM stay in-process.
A **sdk no-native** job
`cargo check`s `syllabix-core` with `--no-default-features` on a runner
without CMake (`setup-linux.sh` is skipped). A Linux-only **crates.io
package** job runs one `cargo package` for `syllabix-native`,
`syllabix-stt`, `syllabix-tts` and `syllabix-core` with verify. Cargo builds
each crate from its tarball against the other new tarballs, not crates.io
([cargo package](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/commands/cargo-package.html)).
It fails if the native `.crate` is over 10 MB. PR template and
harness-evidence checks also run on hosted Linux.

The **git-consumer** workflow (`git-consumer.yml`) pretends to be another repo.
It depends on `syllabix-core` from git: a `v*` tag when one exists, otherwise
the commit under test. It then compiles
`crates/syllabix-core/examples/embed-loop.rs` and `custom-llm.rs`. Locally, run
`./scripts/ci-git-consumer.sh`.

Weekly CI runs `cargo test --workspace` on Linux / Windows (hosted) and macOS
(self-hosted Apple Silicon), including launch-stack native inference.

The native inference check runs those weights under
`cargo llvm-cov --no-cfg-coverage --release` with
`-p syllabix-core --features native-inference --test native_inference`
(`native-inference` turns on `ggml`; ONNX stays always-on). Reports upload as
`coverage-cobertura-native`. No native percentage floor yet — baseline first
(#174).

# Diagnostics — turn timeline and audio capture

Per-turn instrumentation. Diagnostics are yaml-only (there is no CLI flag);
default `run` records nothing. Measurement protocols, segment definitions,
and p50/p95 targets live in [`reference-profiles.md`](reference-profiles.md)
§10 — this file is the field guide: how to enable, what each anchor means,
and what a real report looks like.

## Enable

```yaml
# syllabix.yaml
diagnostics:
  timestamps: true              # turn-*/turn.json sidecars under `directory`
  audio: true                   # additionally capture/clean/utterance/tts.wav; implies timestamps
  trajectory: true              # additionally turn-*/trajectory.jsonl; implies timestamps
  directory: target/turn-debug  # optional; omit when the default is fine
```

| Configuration | Sidecar | WAVs | Trajectory | PCM buffered |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| block absent / all false | no | no | no | none |
| `timestamps: true` | yes | no | no | none |
| `audio: true` | yes | yes | no | yes |
| `trajectory: true` | yes | no | yes | none |
| `audio: true` + `trajectory: true` | yes | yes | yes | yes |

## Agent trajectory (`trajectory.jsonl`)

With `trajectory: true`, each turn directory also contains `trajectory.jsonl`:
one JSON object per line, in order — the user utterance, every tool call with
its validated arguments, every bounded tool result, the assistant reply, and
the turn outcome. The same `trajectory.jsonl` is written for
`agent_harness.agent: syllabix` and `agent_harness.agent: goose`, so a turn can be read
without knowing the underlying protocol.

```json
{"kind":"user","text":"what are my holdings?"}
{"kind":"tool_call","name":"shell","call_id":"c1","arguments":{"command":"kite holdings"}}
{"kind":"tool_result","name":"shell","call_id":"c1","ok":true,"content":"INFY 10"}
{"kind":"assistant","text":"You hold 10 INFY."}
{"kind":"outcome","outcome":"completed"}
```

`outcome` is `completed`, `skipped`, or `cancelled`. Long arguments and content
are truncated to 4096 bytes. Every string passes through a secret filter before
it is written: literal values of secret-named environment variables
(`SYLLABIX_*_API_KEY`, `KITE_*`, `*_TOKEN`, `*_SECRET`, `*_PASSWORD`) are
removed along with credential-shaped tokens (`Bearer`/`Basic` headers, `sk-…`,
GitHub/Slack/AWS keys, JWTs) and values under sensitive JSON keys such as
`api_key`. Redaction rewrites the exported trajectory copy only; `turn.json`,
the WAVs, and `acp.jsonl` are never rewritten.

With `agent_harness.agent: goose`, `acp.jsonl` remains the raw ACP wire log for deep
debugging; `trajectory.jsonl` is the step list written for every agent.

## Goose transcript (`acp.jsonl`)

With `agent_harness.agent: goose` and diagnostics on, each turn directory may also
contain `acp.jsonl`: one JSON object per line of the conversation between
Syllabix and Goose (`dir` is `in` or `out`, `msg` is the payload). API keys and
other Goose spawn-env secrets are not written. The file is absent when Goose is
not used or diagnostics are off.

## Timeline anchors

Each `turn.json` carries `"timeline"` — monotonic milliseconds from the
turn's SpeechStart, rendered in pipeline order. Anchors the turn never
reached render as `null` (a barge-in-interrupted turn, for example, has no
`llm_last_token_ms`; a turn cut short by quitting may have no
`playback_done_ms` because the speaker never drained).

Provider metadata includes `tts_provider`, `tts_model`, and `tts_backend`.
For Qwen3-TTS, `tts_backend` is the placement confirmed by the startup
warm-up (`metal` or `cpu`), including an automatic CPU fallback.

| Anchor | Captured at |
|---|---|
| `speech_start` | First Silero-positive frame opens the turn (epoch, renders as 0) |
| `speech_end` | VAD hangover satisfied; utterance closed |
| `stt_queued` | STT worker dequeued the utterance |
| `stt_partial` | First visible partial transcript from a streaming STT provider (otherwise `null`) |
| `stt_done` | Transcript text and language ready |
| `llm_start` | LLM worker began generating |
| `llm_first_token` | First token streamed |
| `llm_last_token` | Last token of the generation |
| `tts_first_pcm` | First PCM the TTS worker synthesized (worker-side, including incremental vocoder windows) |
| `tts_last_pcm` | Final PCM chunk |
| `playback_first` | Speaker callback first consumed samples of this turn |
| `playback_done` | Speaker drained after the final chunk (final audible sample) |

Named latency segments (`llm_ttft_ms`, `audible_latency_ms`,
`llm_end_to_first_pcm_ms`, …) are computed from these anchors by
`scripts/summarize-timelines.py`; the formulas are in
[`reference-profiles.md`](reference-profiles.md) §10.

## Capture and summarize

```bash
cargo run -p syllabix --release -- run          # talk ≥20 turns for a real sample
python3 scripts/summarize-timelines.py target/turn-debug   # contributor-only tool
```

Interrupted turns dump immediately as `"outcome": "cancelled"` with whatever
anchors exist, so barge-in captures work with `run --barge-in` too.

## Sample report

Output of `scripts/summarize-timelines.py` over a three-turn live capture:

```text
segment                      n       p50       p95     min     max
------------------------------------------------------------------
user_speech_ms               3      2237      2241    1279    2241
vad_queue_wait_ms            3         0         0       0       0
stt_decode_ms                3       389       411     384     413
stt_total_ms                 3       389       411     384     413
handoff_llm_ms               3         0         0       0       0
llm_ttft_ms                  3       200       255     149     261
llm_stream_ms                3       545       678     229     693
tts_lead_ms                  3      1019      1700     980    1776
llm_end_to_first_pcm_ms      3       790      1187     287    1231
tts_synthesis_ms             3      1339      1788     489    1838
playback_handoff_ms          3        10        11       2      11
audible_latency_ms           3      1595      2352    1563    2436
spoken_duration_ms           0         —         —       —       —
total_turn_ms                0         —         —       —       —

raw anchors (ms from speech_start):
anchor                       n       p50       p95
--------------------------------------------------
speech_start_ms              3         0         0
speech_end_ms                3      2237      2241
stt_queued_ms                3      2237      2241
stt_done_ms                  3      2630      2648
llm_start_ms                 3      2630      2648
llm_first_token_ms           3      2850      2887
llm_last_token_ms            3      3436      3532
tts_first_pcm_ms             3      3830      4583
tts_last_pcm_ms              3      5668      5972
playback_first_ms            3      3832      4592
```

Reading the sample:

- **`n=0` rows are expected when sessions end abruptly.** `spoken_duration_ms`
  and `total_turn_ms` need `playback_done_ms`, which only fires when the
  speaker callback drains after the last chunk — quitting right after a reply
  leaves it `null`. Let the agent finish, wait a beat, then quit if you want
  complete turns.
- **`llm_end_to_first_pcm_ms` is signed by design.** Here it is positive
  (~790 ms p50): first PCM landed *after* the last token, i.e. synthesis
  waited on the text rather than overlapping generation. Negative values mean
  the opposite (sentence streaming started while tokens were still arriving).
- **`vad_queue_wait_ms` / `handoff_llm_ms` ≈ 0** shows the bounded queues are
  not backing up on this machine; sustained non-zero values would point at
  queue sizing or a slow stage upstream.
- **`audible_latency_ms` (~1.6 s p50)** is the silence-end → first
  speaker-audio number; the split above says most of it sits in STT decode
  (~390 ms) plus LLM time-to-first-token (~200 ms) plus TTS lead/synthesis.

# Embed

Other repos can use Syllabix without forking `pipeline.rs`. The default product is still `syllabix run`.

Depend on the library from [crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/syllabix-core). API docs: [docs.rs/syllabix-core](https://docs.rs/syllabix-core).

Only need speech-to-text? Depend on [`syllabix-stt`](../crates/syllabix-stt/README.md) instead. Its features pick the engines, and `remote` alone builds without C++.

Only need text-to-speech? Depend on [`syllabix-tts`](../crates/syllabix-tts/README.md) instead. Its features pick the engines, and `remote` alone builds without C++.

Most apps use the defaults (same as `syllabix run`). The first build compiles the bundled whisper.cpp / llama.cpp with CMake and a C++ compiler ([Host compile](#host-compile)). Nothing is downloaded at build time. Models still download on first run ([Cache](#cache)).

```bash
cargo add syllabix-core
```

```toml
[dependencies]
syllabix-core = "0.1"
```

If your app brings its own speech-to-text, LLM, and text-to-speech, turn the defaults off. Then you don't need CMake:

```toml
[dependencies]
syllabix-core = { version = "0.1", default-features = false }
```

For unreleased changes on `main`, you can still depend on git:

```toml
[dependencies]
syllabix-core = { git = "https://github.com/syllabix-ai/syllabix.git" }
```

To use a released git tag instead of crates.io:

```toml
[dependencies]
syllabix-core = { git = "https://github.com/syllabix-ai/syllabix.git", tag = "v0.1.3" }
```

The `syllabix` CLI is not on crates.io. Install it from a [GitHub Release](https://github.com/syllabix-ai/syllabix/releases) or `cargo install --git` (Lane 1).

## Tags and versions

The SDK (`syllabix-core`), the speech crates (`syllabix-stt`, `syllabix-tts`) and the CLI (`syllabix`) share one version. A git tag `vX.Y.Z` is that version for all of them, the GitHub Release binaries, and the crates.io publish. `syllabix-native` is not a public API; depend on `syllabix-core`, `syllabix-stt` or `syllabix-tts`.

What each release contains is on the git tag and its [GitHub Release](https://github.com/syllabix-ai/syllabix/releases). Maintainers cut tags as described in [contributing — Packaging](contributing.md#packaging-maintainers). Hosts: [Compatibility](#compatibility).

## Compatibility

Depend on `syllabix-core` from crates.io, and read the [GitHub Release](https://github.com/syllabix-ai/syllabix/releases) notes before upgrading.

The supported API is only the freeze lists on this page: [Lane 2](#supported-types-lane-2), [Lane 2 with `full`](#supported-types-lane-2-needs-full), [Lane 3](#supported-types-lane-3-additional), and [Lane 3 with `full`](#supported-types-lane-3-needs-full). These are names that are always at the crate root, plus the ones that exist only with `full`.

CI checks this list.

Items in named modules (`testing`, `g2p`, `sandbox`, and the rest) and the `*_ASSET` constants are **not** covered unless a freeze list names them.

## Three lanes

| Lane | Status | What you do | When it fits |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **1 — Sidecar binary** | Ready | Run a GitHub Release binary (usual) or `cargo install --git`. Put `syllabix.yaml` in the working directory. | Electron / Tauri / Python / CI. No custom STT/LLM. A Release needs no compile; `cargo install --git` does. |
| **2 — Embed the live loop** | Ready | `run_live` / `run_live_with_controls` + `LoopEvent` | In-process Rust host that wants the shipped conversation loop. |
| **3 — Compose stages** | Preview | Implement `Vad` / `Stt` / `Llm` / `Tts` / `AudioCapture` / `AudioSink`, swap them on a `Session`, and run | Bring your own engine (often only the LLM). |

Ready = used by the CLI. Preview = less proven. Depend from crates.io ([Compatibility](#compatibility)).

## Cargo features

`syllabix-core` defaults to the same build as `syllabix run`: local speech engines, microphone and speakers, and the online LLM adapter. With `default-features = false` you get `run_loop`, the provider traits, `Session`, and the in-memory stages under `syllabix_core::testing` if you supply every stage yourself. That path does not run CMake and does not compile whisper.cpp / llama.cpp.

| Feature | On by default? | Who should enable it | What it turns on |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `full` | yes (`default`) | Lane 2, and Lane 3 hosts that still use shipped engines or the real mic/speakers | `ggml` + `device-audio` + `cloud`. `run_live`, `load_real_providers`, and `Session` defaults. |
| `ggml` | via `full` | Lane 3 that still loads this crate’s Whisper / local LLM / Qwen engines | Optional `syllabix-native` (CMake + C++). |
| `device-audio` | via `full` | Lane 3 that still uses the real microphone and speakers | Device I/O and echo cancellation (`NativeCapture` / `NativePlayback`). |
| `cloud` | via `full` | Hosts whose yaml uses `pipeline.llm.provider: openai-compatible`, `pipeline.stt.provider: online`, or `pipeline.tts.provider: online` with `load_real_providers` | `LiveLlm::Cloud`, `LiveStt::Remote`, and `LiveTts::Remote` in the real loader. `openai::OpenAiLlm` always compiles; `remote_stt::RemoteStt` and `remote_tts::RemoteTts` need this feature. |
| `native-inference` | no | Contributors running the slow model tests (`native_inference`) | Turns on `ggml` plus the tests that download and run the real models (GGUF and ONNX). ONNX (`ort`) is always built in; this feature does not switch it on. |

**Lane 3 that implements every stage** (see `examples/custom-llm.rs`): `default-features = false`.  
**Lane 3 that swaps only the LLM and keeps the other defaults:** keep `full` (or at least `ggml` + `device-audio`). That still compiles whisper.cpp.  
**Lane 2 `run_live`:** `full` (or `ggml` + `device-audio`).

Do not enable `ggml` unless you have the [Host compile](#host-compile) toolchain. Hosts should not enable `native-inference`.

## Lane 1 — Sidecar binary

The usual Lane 1 install is a [GitHub Release](https://github.com/syllabix-ai/syllabix/releases) binary ([install](install.md)). You download a file and run it. You do not compile.

If this machine already has a C++ compiler and CMake, you can instead install from a git tag:

```bash
cargo install --git https://github.com/syllabix-ai/syllabix.git --tag v0.1.3 syllabix
```

Always pass `--tag vX.Y.Z`. Do not install from `main`. This builds the on-device speech libraries, so you need the packages under [Host compile](#host-compile) (same list: [install — Compile](install.md#compile)). More notes: [install — Install from git](install.md#install-from-git).

**Contract**

| Piece | What hosts may rely on |
| --- | --- |
| CLI | `syllabix run`, `syllabix run --barge-in`, `syllabix init [DIR]`, `syllabix --help`. Full list: [cli](cli.md). |
| Config | Optional `syllabix.yaml` in the process working directory. Missing file uses built-ins. Keys: [syllabix.yaml](syllabix-yaml.md). |
| Environment | `SYLLABIX_LLM_API_KEY` for `pipeline.llm.provider: openai-compatible` (never yaml). `SYLLABIX_STT_API_KEY` for online STT. `SYLLABIX_TTS_API_KEY` for online TTS. `SYLLABIX_CACHE_DIR` to share or relocate the model cache. |
| Exit codes | `0` success. `1` I/O, config, device, cache, cancel, provider, or pipeline failure. `2` command not implemented. |

`--help` and `init` download nothing. First `run` of the default stack fetches about 2.5 GB into the cache (below).

## Lane 2 — Embed the live loop

The host compiles the C++ speech libraries ([Host compile](#host-compile)), shares the model cache ([Cache](#cache)), and must carry Apache-2.0 plus Sonora BSD in its NOTICE.

```rust
use syllabix_core::{run_live, AgentConfig, Cancel};

fn main() -> syllabix_core::Result<()> {
    let config = AgentConfig::resolve_for_run(&std::env::current_dir()?)?;
    run_live(&config, Cancel::new(), None, false)?;
    Ok(())
}
```

The minimal call above is covered by `crates/syllabix-core/examples/embed-loop.rs`: a CI-checked fuller copy that also subscribes to `LoopEvent` and reports `LoopReport` (`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` compiles examples, so the supported API cannot bitrot).

`AgentConfig::v0()` is the same zero-config stack as a missing yaml file. Pass `true` as the last argument of `run_live` for barge-in. Subscribe to `LoopEvent` with `std::sync::mpsc::channel` when you need a UI. For a live handle, call `run_live_with_controls(config, cancel, Some(tx), controls)`.

`run_live` fails fast on a missing `SYLLABIX_LLM_API_KEY` when yaml selects an online LLM, before devices or weights load.

### Supported types (Lane 2)

Treat only this list as the supported crate-root surface. Other public items live in named modules (`syllabix_core::testing`, `syllabix_core::g2p`, `syllabix_core::sandbox`, and the rest) and are not a stability promise. New crate-root re-exports still need a line on this page before they land ([contributing](contributing.md#supported-library-api)). `crates/syllabix-core/tests/supported_api.rs` fails if a crate-root `pub use` is missing from these tables, or if a freeze-list name leaves the crate root.

| Type / function | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `AgentConfig` | Validated yaml / built-in stack (`v0`, `resolve_for_run`, `load_path`, `parse_yaml`). |
| `Cancel` | Shutdown and in-flight generation cancel. |
| `RuntimeControls` | Barge-in and mic mute while the loop is running. |
| `LoopEvent` | Ready, user/partial/assistant text, thinking, AEC, tools, timings, playback. |
| `LoopReport` | Completed turns, queue occupancy, cancelled/skipped. |
| `Error` / `Result` | Recoverable failures; `Error::exit_code` matches the CLI. |
| `ModelCache` / `cache_root` | First-run weight cache (`ModelCache::v0()` is the product cache). |

### Supported types (Lane 2, needs `full`)

These crate-root names exist only when the `full` feature is on (`ggml` + `device-audio`). They are still the supported Lane 2 surface.

| Type / function | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `run_live` | Load weights, open default mic/speakers, run until shutdown or capture ends (`config`, `Cancel`, `Option<Sender<LoopEvent>>`, barge-in `bool`). |
| `run_live_with_controls` | `run_live_with_controls(config, cancel, Some(tx), controls)`. |

## Lane 3 — Compose stages

Build a `Session` from yaml (`Session::from_config`) or `Session::v0()`.
Stages you do not set load like `run_live`: Silero, the configured
speech-to-text / language model / text-to-speech from the cache, native
mic and speakers. Swap only the stages you own.

```rust
use syllabix_core::{AgentConfig, Cancel, Session};

let config = AgentConfig::resolve_for_run(&std::env::current_dir()?)?;
Session::from_config(&config)
    .with_llm(EchoLlm)
    .run(Cancel::new())?;
```

You do not wire `load_real_providers`, `HttpFetcher`, or `NativeCapture`
by hand. Those still exist if you want the lower-level seam; see
[`real.rs`](../crates/syllabix-core/src/real.rs).

```rust
use syllabix_core::{Cancel, Llm, Result, TokenChunk, Transcript};

struct EchoLlm;

impl Llm for EchoLlm {
    fn name(&self) -> &'static str {
        "echo"
    }

    fn generate(
        &mut self,
        _history: &[syllabix_core::HistoryTurn],
        user: &Transcript,
        cancel: &Cancel,
        on_token: &mut dyn FnMut(TokenChunk) -> Result<()>,
    ) -> Result<()> {
        if cancel.is_shutdown() {
            return Err(syllabix_core::Error::Cancelled);
        }
        on_token(TokenChunk {
            turn: user.turn,
            generation: cancel.generation(),
            index: 0,
            text: user.text.clone(),
            is_last: true,
        })
    }
}
```

The trait impl above is covered by `crates/syllabix-core/examples/custom-llm.rs`. That file uses in-memory fixtures so CI can run without a microphone (`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` compiles examples, so the supported API cannot bitrot). A host that swaps only the LLM and keeps the other `Session` defaults still needs the `ggml` and `device-audio` features (on by default). Skipping CMake is only for hosts that supply every stage themselves.

A yaml `pipeline.llm.provider: openai-compatible` still needs `SYLLABIX_LLM_API_KEY` when the LLM slot is the default. A custom `Llm` does not. Native mic/speaker types live under `syllabix_core::audio` and are **not** in the Lane 2 freeze list.

### Supported types (Lane 3, additional)

| Type / function | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `Session` | Builder: defaults for every stage; `with_vad` / `with_stt` / `with_llm` / `with_tts` / `with_capture` / `with_sink` / `with_frames` then `run`. |
| `Vad`, `Stt`, `Llm`, `Tts` | Pipeline stages. |
| `AudioCapture`, `AudioSink` | Mic (or fixture) and speakers (or collector). |
| `run_loop` / `run_loop_captured` | In-memory cascade; blocks until workers join. |
| `PipelineStages`, `LoopConfig` | Arguments to `run_loop`. |
| `AudioFrame` | One PCM frame into VAD or capture. |
| `VadEvent` / `Utterance` / `TurnId` | VAD events and the turn they belong to. |
| `Transcript` / `HistoryTurn` / `TokenChunk` | STT text, chat history, and LLM stream chunks. |
| `SynthesizedAudio` | TTS audio for the sink. |

Do not fork `pipeline.rs`. Swap a trait impl instead.

### Supported types (Lane 3, needs `full`)

`load_real_providers` is crate-root only with the `ggml` feature (on via `full`).

| Type / function | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `load_real_providers` | Silero + configured STT/LLM/TTS from the cache. |

## Host compile

If you embed Syllabix in your own Rust app (Lane 2 or Lane 3), your machine compiles the C++ speech libraries that ship with Syllabix (whisper.cpp / llama.cpp). The source is bundled in the crate; nothing is downloaded at build time. You need CMake and a C++ compiler. The first compile takes several minutes. Lane 3 hosts that set `default-features = false` and supply every stage themselves skip that compile. If you only run a downloaded Syllabix binary (Lane 1), skip this section. A Lane 1 `cargo install --git` build compiles the CLI, so it needs the same packages ([install — Install from git](install.md#install-from-git)).

Same packages as [install — Compile](install.md#compile). This repo’s Linux setup script also installs extra tools used only in our tests; those are called out below.

| You need | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Rust 1.91 or newer | Pinned in this repo. |
| CMake and a C++ compiler | Builds the speech libraries. First compile takes several minutes. |
| Linux: `pkg-config` and ALSA headers (`libasound2-dev`) | Mic and speakers on Linux. |
| macOS: Xcode Command Line Tools | Apple’s C++ compiler. GPU libraries link on their own. |
| Windows: Visual C++ build tools, Windows SDK, and CMake | Open an x64 Native Tools prompt so `cl.exe` is on `PATH`. |

**Linux (Debian / Ubuntu)**

```bash
sudo apt-get install -y build-essential cmake pkg-config libasound2-dev
```

In a Syllabix checkout you can run `./scripts/setup-linux.sh` instead. That script also installs `git` and `bubblewrap`. You do not need those two just to depend on `syllabix-core` from another repo.

**macOS** — Install Xcode Command Line Tools, CMake (Homebrew `cmake` if needed), and rustup. Put rustup’s `cargo` ahead of Homebrew’s. In a Syllabix checkout you can run `./scripts/setup-macos.sh`.

**Windows** — Install [Visual Studio Build Tools](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/visual-cpp-build-tools/) with **Desktop development with C++**, [CMake](https://cmake.org/download/) on `PATH`, and rustup. Open an x64 Native Tools prompt, then build.

Optional: Linux Vulkan is `SYLLABIX_GGML_VULKAN=1` (needs Vulkan headers). Default Linux and Windows builds use CPU.

## Cache

The first run of the default models downloads about **2.5 GB** (Silero, Whisper `small`, LFM3-1.7B, Pocket TTS). Files are fetched over HTTPS, checked, then reused. `--help` and `init` download nothing. Other yaml model ids download the first time you use that id. Full list: [engines](engines.md).

Files always go in `<cache-root>/models/v1`.

| When | Cache root | Files |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SYLLABIX_CACHE_DIR` is set | that folder | `$SYLLABIX_CACHE_DIR/models/v1` |
| else `$XDG_CACHE_HOME` is set | `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/syllabix` | `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/syllabix/models/v1` |
| else on Windows | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\syllabix\cache` | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\syllabix\cache\models\v1` |
| else `$HOME` is set | `~/.cache/syllabix` | `~/.cache/syllabix/models/v1` |
| else | `.syllabix-cache` in the current directory | `.syllabix-cache/models/v1` |

Set `SYLLABIX_CACHE_DIR` to the **cache root**, not to `models/v1`. Two apps share downloads when they use the same root: leave the variable unset (same user default) or set the same path in every process.

# Engines

The ids you can put in `syllabix.yaml`. Key syntax: [syllabix.yaml](syllabix-yaml.md). Measured timings: [workload benchmark](workload_benchmark/workload_benchmark.md). Licenses of fetched weights: [NOTICE](../NOTICE).

Weights download on first use of each id (HTTPS URL pinned in the binary, SHA-256 check, then reuse from cache). Default `run` fetches only the launch stack: Silero, Whisper `small`, LFM3-1.7B, Pocket TTS (~2.5 GB). `--help` and `init` download nothing.

Cache path (files land in `models/v1` under the cache root), first match wins:

- `$SYLLABIX_CACHE_DIR/models/v1` if `SYLLABIX_CACHE_DIR` is set (that variable is the cache root, not `models/v1`)
- else `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/syllabix/models/v1`
- else, on Windows, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\syllabix\cache\models\v1`
- else `~/.cache/syllabix/models/v1`
- else `.syllabix-cache/models/v1` (cwd)

Share downloads across the CLI and embed hosts by leaving the variable unset or pointing every process at the same root. Details: [embed — Cache](embed.md#cache).

## Machine needs

| | What ships / what is known |
| --- | --- |
| **Release artifacts** | Linux x64, macOS Apple Silicon, Windows x64. Intel Macs are not supported. |
| **Default cache** | ~2.5 GB on first `run` |
| **Compute** | Darwin: Metal + Accelerate for STT/LLM. Linux/Windows: portable CPU by default. Opt-in Linux Vulkan builds (`SYLLABIX_GGML_VULKAN=1`) offload whisper/llama/Qwen when a device is present. Qwen TTS/ASR stay CPU unless `compute` selects Metal/Vulkan (or Auto probes them). |
| **RAM** | Not a published gate. The default stack is the combination measured for an Apple M4 / 16 GiB class machine; see [reference profiles](reference-profiles.md). |
| **Network** | First fetch of each id needs HTTPS. After the cache is full, default `run` needs none. |

Select with `pipeline.tts.model: indic-mio`; only `hi-female`, `hi-male`, and `ta-female` speaker embeddings ship in-tree. Weights download on first use. See [NOTICE](../crates/syllabix-tts/NOTICE). | https://huggingface.co/bytepass0/indic-mio-q8-gguf |

`pipeline.tts.provider: online` posts each finished sentence to OpenAI-compatible `POST /v1/audio/speech` (`stream_format=audio`). No TTS weights are fetched. Key: `SYLLABIX_TTS_API_KEY`. A self-hosted worker: [`syllabix serve tts`](cli.md#serve). Yaml: [local vs online](syllabix-yaml.md#local-vs-online).

Hosted endpoints that speak this Audio REST (not OpenAI Realtime): [OpenAI speech-to-text](https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/speech-to-text) / [text-to-speech](https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/text-to-speech), [Groq speech-to-text](https://console.groq.com/docs/speech-to-text) / [text-to-speech](https://console.groq.com/docs/text-to-speech), [whisper.cpp whisper-server](https://github.com/ggml-org/whisper.cpp/tree/master/examples/server), [Kokoro-FastAPI](https://github.com/remsky/Kokoro-FastAPI). Default `run` stays local. Yaml: [local vs online](syllabix-yaml.md#local-vs-online).

## S2S (speech-to-speech)

Local speech-to-speech is not an STT, LLM, or TTS menu id. Select it with `pipeline.mode: s2s` and `pipeline.s2s.model` — [syllabix.yaml](syllabix-yaml.md#pipeline-mode--cascade-vs-s2s). Default `run` without that yaml stays cascade.

| Yaml `pipeline.s2s.model` | Notes | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `lfm3-audio-2b` | English-only experimental voice chat (LFM 1.0). The turn uses the model’s default GGUF chat template in mixed text+audio mode ([Voice chat](https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/LFM3-Audio-2B#voice-chat-speech-and-text-responses)). Weights fetch on first s2s run only. Indic / code-switched voice chat remains the cascade path (Hima, Indic-Mio, and related ids). | [model card](https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/LFM3-Audio-2B), [GGUF repo](https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/LFM3-Audio-2B-GGUF), [NOTICE](../NOTICE) |

Silero VAD still commits each user turn. `run --barge-in` still interrupts playback on user speech; this path is turn-based, not full duplex. Assistant replies stay in the conversation until the context is full; a barged-in reply is closed in-cache so the next user turn can continue. Loop diagram: [architecture](architecture.md#speech-to-speech-pipelinemode-s2s).

Contributor pins, ggml patches, and llama-bench: [contributing.md](contributing.md#models).

# FAQ

Symptom fixes (won't verify, Gatekeeper, no mic, self-interrupt): [troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md).

## Why is the first `run` so large / slow?

Default `run` fetches Silero, Whisper `small`, LFM3-1.7B, and Pocket TTS (~2.5 GB), then checks SHA-256. How long that takes depends on network bandwidth. Later runs reuse the cache offline. `--help` and `init` download nothing.

## Memory is tight. Can I use a smaller model?

Yes. `syllabix init`, then either set `pipeline.llm.model` to `lfm2.5-350m` or `lfm2.5-230m`, or set `pipeline.llm.provider: openai-compatible` with `base_url` and `SYLLABIX_LLM_API_KEY` so the LLM runs in the cloud (transcript text only; mic audio stays local). Catalogue and keys: [engines](engines.md), [syllabix.yaml](syllabix-yaml.md).

## Why is barge-in off by default?

The default finishes the agent's sentence so open-speaker echo cannot cut it off mid-word. Pass `run --barge-in` when you want talk-over, or enable it during the conversation via the terminal UI (`b`). AEC is still on in both modes.

## Do I need headphones?

Not if AEC holds on your laptop speakers. Let the ~10 s calibration finish before talking. If the agent still treats its own voice as yours, use headphones and report the device names from the startup line.

## Where do API keys go?

Nowhere in yaml, and nowhere in a `.env` file. Online LLM uses `SYLLABIX_LLM_API_KEY`; online STT uses `SYLLABIX_STT_API_KEY`; online TTS uses `SYLLABIX_TTS_API_KEY`. Default local `run` needs no key.

## Download or compile?

Download a Release binary if you just want to talk — that is the usual install. Compile (`cargo run -p syllabix -- run`) if you are changing the code. To put a tagged CLI on your `PATH` without cloning, see [install from git](install.md#install-from-git).

## Can I change the voice / model without rebuilding?

Yes. `syllabix init`, edit `pipeline.*.model` in `syllabix.yaml`. Catalogue: [engines](engines.md). Unknown ids fail at load.

## Does audio leave the machine?

No, not for a normal local `run` after the models are already downloaded. An online LLM sends only the transcript text. Online STT sends each finished clip as a WAV file; online TTS sends each finished sentence. The live microphone stays on this computer. `syllabix serve` puts the models on a shared worker; each desk still sends only those clips or sentences, not the live mic. Details: [architecture](architecture.md#what-leaves-the-machine), [CLI serve](cli.md#serve), [engines](engines.md#tts).

```bash
curl -L https://github.com/syllabix-ai/syllabix/releases/latest/download/syllabix-$(uname -s)-$(uname -m) -o syllabix
```

```powershell
.\syllabix.exe run
```

`uname -s` / `uname -m` map to the names below (`Linux`/`x86_64`, `Darwin`/`arm64`). Intel Macs are not supported.

| Computer | File to download |
| --- | --- |
| Linux x64 | `syllabix-Linux-x86_64` |
| macOS Apple Silicon | `syllabix-Darwin-arm64` |

## Install from git

The usual install is still the GitHub Release binary above. Use that if you only want to run `syllabix`.

If this machine already has CMake, a C++ compiler, and (on Linux) ALSA, you can instead build the CLI from a git tag:

```bash
cargo install --git https://github.com/syllabix-ai/syllabix.git --tag v0.1.3 syllabix
```

The last word (`syllabix`) is the crate that provides the `syllabix` binary. Always pass `--tag vX.Y.Z`. Do not install from `main` or a branch. Cargo puts the binary on your PATH (`~/.cargo/bin/syllabix` unless `CARGO_HOME` is set).

This build needs the same packages as [Compile](#compile). Projects that embed the library list them under [embed — Host compile](embed.md#host-compile). The first `run` still downloads models; see [First run](#first-run).

## First run

The first `run` downloads the default models over HTTPS: Silero, Whisper `small`, LFM3-1.7B, and Pocket TTS (about **2.5 GB**). Each file is checked, then stored under the cache root:

| When | Asset directory |
| --- | --- |
| `SYLLABIX_CACHE_DIR` set | `$SYLLABIX_CACHE_DIR/models/v1` |
| else `$XDG_CACHE_HOME` set | `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/syllabix/models/v1` |
| else Windows | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\syllabix\cache\models\v1` |
| else `$HOME` set | `~/.cache/syllabix/models/v1` |
| else | `.syllabix-cache/models/v1` (cwd) |

`SYLLABIX_CACHE_DIR` is the cache root, not the `models/v1` folder. Leave it unset to share the per-user default across the CLI and any host that embeds `syllabix-core`, or set the same root in every process. Hosts: [embed — Cache](embed.md#cache).

Later runs reuse the cache offline. `--help` and `init` do not download weights. Other yaml model ids fetch on first use of that id. Catalogue: [engines.md](engines.md).


## Compile

Requires Rust 1.91+ (pinned in `rust-toolchain.toml`), CMake, and a C++ compiler. whisper.cpp and llama.cpp share one `ggml` compiled into the binary (Darwin Metal + Accelerate; Linux/Windows portable CPU by default). Vendored trees ship in the repo — no git submodules. Linux also needs ALSA headers (`libasound2-dev`) and `pkg-config`. Other repos that embed `syllabix-core` (Lane 2 / Lane 3) need this same compile toolchain — [embed — Host compile](embed.md#host-compile).

### Compile dependencies

#### Linux (Debian / Ubuntu)

```bash
./scripts/setup-linux.sh
```

Installs `build-essential`, `cmake`, `pkg-config`, `libasound2-dev`, `git`, and `bubblewrap`, then rustup if missing. CI Linux jobs run this same script. Optional Vulkan toolchain packages: `./scripts/setup-linux.sh --with-vulkan`, then `SYLLABIX_GGML_VULKAN=1 cargo build -p syllabix --release`. Vulkan details: [`crates/syllabix-native/vendor/README.md`](../crates/syllabix-native/vendor/README.md).

On Ubuntu 24.04+, if `bwrap --unshare-net` fails during sandbox tests, see [contributing.md](contributing.md) / CI (`kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=0`).

#### macOS

```bash
./scripts/setup-macos.sh
```

Ensures Xcode Command Line Tools, installs CMake via Homebrew when needed, and rustup if missing. CI macOS jobs run this same script. Prefer rustup’s `cargo`/`rustc` over Homebrew’s (`"${CARGO_HOME:-$HOME/.cargo}/bin"` first on `PATH`). Metal and Accelerate link automatically.

#### Windows

1. Install [Visual Studio Build Tools](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/visual-cpp-build-tools/) (or full VS) with the **Desktop development with C++** workload (MSVC + Windows SDK).
2. Install [CMake](https://cmake.org/download/) and ensure `cmake` is on `PATH`.
3. Install [rustup](https://rustup.rs/) for the `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` toolchain.
4. Open **x64 Native Tools Command Prompt for VS** (or a Developer PowerShell) so `cl.exe` is visible, then build from that environment.

```powershell
rustc --version
cmake --version
where.exe cl
```

### Build and run

```bash

cd syllabix
```

# Issues

## Bugs and features

Open a public issue: https://github.com/syllabix-ai/syllabix/issues/new/choose

Pick the matching template:

- Audio / conversation — mic, speakers, echo, barge-in, STT, or spoken reply.
- Install / first open — binary will not verify, open, or fetch models.
- Config / yaml — `syllabix.yaml` keys, models, online LLM, diagnostics.

Check [troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md) and [FAQ](faq.md) first — mic, echo, keys, and first-run fetch are covered there.

Include in every report:

- Syllabix version or git SHA, and OS (macOS Apple Silicon, Linux x64, Windows x64). Intel Macs are not supported.
- Artifact or how you installed (Release file name, or `cargo run`).
- Exact command and full error text.
- `syllabix.yaml` when used. Never paste API keys — `SYLLABIX_LLM_API_KEY` is environment-only.
- For audio reports: mic and speaker names from the startup line, barge-in on/off, and diagnostics (`turn.json` plus `utterance.wav` / `clean.wav` / `tts.wav` when not private) — see [diagnostics](diagnostics.md).

## Security

Syllabix is a local voice agent. The default `run` path keeps microphone audio on the machine after the model cache is filled. Optional online stages send only what that stage needs (LLM: transcript text; STT: utterance WAV; TTS: sentence text). Keys stay in the environment (`SYLLABIX_LLM_API_KEY` / `SYLLABIX_STT_API_KEY` / `SYLLABIX_TTS_API_KEY`), never yaml or a `.env` file.

Do **not** open a public GitHub issue for a security bug, a leaked key, or a sandbox escape.

Use GitHub's private advisory form:

https://github.com/syllabix-ai/syllabix/security/advisories/new

Include the Syllabix version or git SHA, OS, and the shortest steps that reproduce the problem.

### What is in scope

- Unexpected network use on the default local stack after the cache is full
- Secrets appearing in yaml, logs, diagnostics sidecars, or spoken output
- Sandbox / agent-harness escapes (write, network, or secret access beyond the configured ceiling)

### What is not a vulnerability

- First `run` downloading SHA-pinned model weights over HTTPS
- Unsigned macOS / Windows binaries until release signing exists — see [install](install.md)
- Model quality, latency, or echo on a given laptop

# Reference test profiles and measurement protocols

How Syllabix measures conversation quality. This is the measurement lab,
not the user README. Every number claimed in a product PR must come from a
command in this file, on one of the profiles below. Launch gates that
still need human machines (signed macOS artifacts, Windows first-open,
measured cold start, end-to-end latency p50/p95) stay empty until someone
runs the protocol — do not invent them in user-facing docs.

## 1. Reference profiles

| Profile | Hardware | Role |
|---|---|---|
| **A — MacBook Air** | Apple Silicon laptop, built-in microphone and speakers at 48 kHz, no headphones, quiet room | The echo/barge-in/3-minute gate. Full-duplex AEC3 is only honest on open speakers; headphones hide self-echo. |
| **B — Linux x64** | GitHub runner or contributor box, ALSA null / no devices, `libasound2-dev` installed | The merge bar: fmt/clippy/release link/dylibs/one-ggml, llvm-cov ≥85% without native weights, `cargo test --workspace` with native inference once. |
| **C — Clean machine** | Any OS image with **no rustc/cargo/python**, network available for the first download only | The scripted README smoke (`scripts/smoke-setup.sh`) and the human 3-minute spoken-reply gate after a Release exists. |

Windows x64 has no profile owner yet: weekly CI compiles it
(`weekly.yml` matrix), but nobody has measured audio quality on it.
Say so in PRs rather than assuming Linux numbers transfer. Intel Macs
are not supported.

## 2. Echo — AEC zero false turns (profile A)

The launch gate. The mic stays open; nothing is muted.

```bash
cargo test -p syllabix-core --test audio_io \
  hardware_aec_1_minute_playback_has_zero_false_turns \
  -- --ignored --exact --nocapture
```

Protocol: 10 s automatic calibration, then 1 minute of looping
`tests/fixtures/vad/speech.wav` on built-in speakers while nobody talks.
**Pass = 0 Silero `SpeechStart` events.** Debug dumps land in
`$SYLLABIX_AEC_DEBUG_DIR` or `target/aec-debug`
(`render.wav`, `capture.wav`, `clean.wav`, sidecar).

Do not pass this by muting capture during playback, adding DeepFilterNet,
or raising Silero threshold/min-speech.

## 3. Barge-in p95 interrupt latency (profile A)

Enable diagnostics in the project's `syllabix.yaml` (field guide:
[`diagnostics.md`](diagnostics.md)), then run with the flag:

```yaml
diagnostics:
  timestamps: true
  audio: true
  directory: target/turn-debug
```

```bash
cargo run -p syllabix --release -- run --barge-in
```

While the agent speaks, talk over it repeatedly. With diagnostics enabled each
interrupted turn dumps the interrupted TTS plus your new utterance.

Measurement: timestamped speech-onset event → playback silence. Launch gate
is **<200 ms at p95 across 100 scripted interruptions per reference OS
profile**. Scripted cancel/flush/preroll behavior is covered by unit tests
(`barge_in_*`, `cancel_*` in syllabix-core/syllabix); the live p95 on open
speakers needs profile A and stays recorded in the launch evidence until a
human runs it.

Without `--barge-in`, VAD SpeechStart during TTS must **not** cancel
playback — that difference is itself a test
(`parses_run_barge_in*`, flag-off cancellation tests).

## 4. Spoken-text quality

- **Intelligibility:** text → Kokoro → Whisper `small` → text must reach
  ≥80 % in-order word match (`TTS_ASR_MIN_WORD_MATCH`). Non-silent PCM is
  not acceptance.
- **Markdown:** headings, list markers, emphasis, links are stripped before
  TTS (`markdown_fixtures_remove_headings_lists_and_emphasis`,
  `markdown_is_stripped_before_synthesis`).
- **Chain of thought:** `<think>…</think>` is stripped before TTS and hidden
  in the TUI even when yaml enables `thinking: true`.
- **Empty turns:** empty or whitespace STT never starts LLM/TTS
  (`empty_utterance_is_rejected_before_decode`).

## 5. Latency lines

The TUI reports STT, TTFT, TTFB, and total per turn (legacy enqueue-based
clocks, unchanged since row 25). The finer, device-true numbers come from the
row-34 timeline sidecars — see §10. Record them from profile A runs when
claiming speedups; do not quote wall-clock numbers from CI. LLM tok/s
comparisons belong in `crates/syllabix-native/vendor/llama-bench.md`.

## 6. Coverage and native inference (profile B)

```bash
cargo llvm-cov --workspace --fail-under-lines 85 --fail-under-file-lines 85 \
  --cobertura --output-path coverage.xml
cargo test --workspace   # last; launch-stack native inference runs here exactly once
```

llvm-cov sets `--cfg coverage` and must not load whisper.cpp / llama.cpp /
native TTS weights or open devices. The floor is 85% workspace lines and 85% in
every reported `src/**/*.rs` file. Production-only native modules are excluded
by the coverage configuration; pure helpers remain in the normal modules.

Weekly native coverage (separate from the unit gate; see #174) measures
production native providers with real weights. `--features native-inference`
turns on `ggml` plus those tests; ONNX (`ort`) is always built in.

```bash
SYLLABIX_NATIVE_MODELS=whisper-small,lfm2.5-230m,pocket-tts \
  cargo llvm-cov --no-cfg-coverage --release \
    -p syllabix-core --features native-inference --test native_inference \
    --cobertura --output-path coverage-native.xml
```

CI runs that lane via `native-tests.yml` on `ubuntu-latest` by default
(pull requests, pushes to `main`, and `workflow_dispatch`). No native
percentage floor yet. The same workflow’s **native serve** job points
the six-turn loop at local [`serve`](cli.md#serve) STT and TTS workers.

## 7. 3-minute gate (profile C)

After a published GitHub Release:

```bash
SMOKE_RELEASE_URL=https://github.com/syllabix-ai/syllabix/releases/download/<tag> \
  scripts/smoke-setup.sh syllabix-Linux-x86_64    # per OS you can touch
```

covers checksum verify, clean-toolchain `--help`, `init`, and the offline
second run. The spoken part stays human: download on the clean machine,
`./syllabix run`, talk, then block the network and confirm a second `run`
still works. Cold-start wall time (binary on disk → first spoken reply) is
recorded here when measured; the user README must not claim three minutes
until that row is filled.

## 8. TTS provider compute placement (row 31, profile A)

Qwen TTS uses adaptive placement on Apple Silicon. After STT and LLM are
resident, `compute: auto` attempts the full Metal voice-anchor warm-up. If
the audio graph cannot reserve or execute its buffers, the Metal context is
destroyed and Qwen is reloaded on CPU. Other operating systems select CPU;
`compute: cpu` and `compute: metal` make either choice explicit. Pocket TTS
remains the zero-config default, so its startup path does not run this probe.

The fallback matters because the audio gen_code graph asks for a ~870 MiB
Metal compute buffer that `ggml_backend_sched` could not place with the
reference STT and LLM contexts resident. Allocation errors are propagated
through mtmd rather than discovered on the first spoken reply. Diagnostics
record the resulting backend as `tts_backend`; component benchmark JSONL
records the same choice as `backend`. STT and LLM JSONL lines use the same
`backend` vocabulary for ggml placement (`cpu` / `metal` / `vulkan`). The run
fingerprint also stores `ggml_backend` (and GPU name / VRAM when known) so a
CPU contribution and a Vulkan contribution on one host hash to different
`docs/eval/runs/<fingerprint>.jsonl` paths.

Protocol (llama-bench at the vendored llama.cpp commit `ad1de39`, 4 threads,
pp512 / tg128, 2 repetitions, MacBook Air Apple Silicon):

```bash
llama-bench -m Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct-Q4_K_M.gguf   -p 512 -n 128 -t 4 -r 2 -ngl 99,0
llama-bench -m Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-Base-Q4_K_M.gguf -p 512 -n 128 -t 4 -r 2 -ngl 0,99
```

| Model | backend | pp512 t/s | tg128 t/s |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Llama 3.2 1B Q4_K_M (LLM slot) | Metal, BLAS | 1137.9 ± 160.6 | 106.3 ± 2.0 |
| Llama 3.2 1B Q4_K_M | CPU | 299.3 ± 8.0 | 81.2 ± 1.7 |
| Qwen3-TTS 1.7B Q4_K_M (TTS slot) | CPU | 832.0 ± 28.5 | **91.5 ± 0.7** |
| Qwen3-TTS 1.7B Q4_K_M | Metal (solo reference) | 220.2 ± 4.0 | 74.7 ± 0.3 |

Read: the LLM slot is ~31% faster at generation on Metal and stays there;
this isolated Qwen TTS *backbone* measurement is ~22% faster on CPU than on
Metal. The complete audio graph is a different axis. On the same M4 16 GiB
host, a release `bench-tts-worker` with explicit `pipeline.tts.compute`
(Qwen alone in the process — no resident STT/LLM) recorded:

| Model | `compute` | mean RTF | mean elapsed | mean audio |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `qwen3-0.6` | `cpu` | 1.331 | 6627 ms | 5360 ms |
| `qwen3-0.6` | `metal` | **0.662** | 4157 ms | 6400 ms |
| `qwen3-1.7` | `cpu` | 1.418 | 8019 ms | 5920 ms |
| `qwen3-1.7` | `metal` | **0.766** | 4465 ms | 5920 ms |

`backend` in the JSONL matched the requested placement. Metal mean RTF is
about 2× the CPU figure and below 1, so isolated synthesis is faster than
the audio it produces. That is compatible with a live turn when the LLM is
`provider: online` (no local GGUF occupying Metal) or when local STT+LLM
leave enough unified memory for the ~870 MiB audio graph; `compute: auto`
still falls back to CPU when that graph cannot reserve. These rows are not
a resident-stack measurement.

`scripts/contribute-performance.sh` needs no change for this. It already
runs isolated TTS workers through `syllabix bench`. On this branch those
workers inherit `compute: auto`, which selects Metal on Apple Silicon when
the solo warm-up succeeds, and records `backend` on each JSONL line.
Forced CPU vs Metal comparison uses yaml `compute: cpu` or `compute: metal`
and `bench-tts-worker --model qwen3-0.6` (same for `qwen3-1.7`); the
contribute script does not take a compute flag.

Sentence-level TTFB/RTF for the qwen provider also still land via the
opt-in native capture (CPU-pinned unless the test is updated to pass
`TtsCompute`):

```bash
SYLLABIX_CACHE_DIR=<cache> SYLLABIX_NATIVE_LATENCY=1 \
  SYLLABIX_NATIVE_MODELS=qwen3-0.6,qwen3-1.7 \
  cargo test --release -p syllabix-core --test native_inference \
  qwen_latency_capture -- --nocapture
```

Run it `--release`: a debug-profile build compiles ggml unoptimized and
produces meaningless RTF (measured ~50x audio time in debug).

## 9. Qwen3-TTS backbone menu and voice pinning (row 32, profile A)

Row 32 adds `qwen3-0.6` alongside the row-31 `qwen3-1.7` under
`pipeline.tts.model`. Each backbone pairs with its own mmproj: the upstream
speech-tokenizer *encoder* weights are byte-identical across sizes, but the
mmproj also carries the projector into the LM embedding space (2048-d for
1.7B, 1024-d for 0.6B) — pairing across sizes fails at load with an
n_embd mismatch. Both 0.6B files (backbone Q4_K_M + mmproj Q8_0) ship from
the community conversion at `mradermacher/Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-0.6B-Base-GGUF`,
sha256-pinned in the manifest; they must pass the same native gates as the
1.7B weight — round-trip ≥80%, numbers gate, cancel <5 s, first sentence
before completion.

**Voice pinning:** the Base backbones are speaker-unconditioned, so every
cold-start generation used to sample a new speaker — a different voice per
utterance. At load the engine now synthesizes a short anchor clip on a
chain pinned to a fixed seed, encodes it through the mmproj speaker
encoder, and conditions every sentence on that x-vector (`speaker_ref`).
Fixed anchor seed ⇒ the same Syllabix voice across sentences, runs, and
backbone sizes; the runtime sampler seed still varies prosody. The machine
proof is `qwen_voice_is_deterministic_under_a_pinned_seed` (two independent
engines, same seed ⇒ identical PCM); speaker consistency itself stays a
human listening-gate item on profile A.

## 10. Turn timeline instrumentation (profile A)

Diagnostics are yaml-only (enable + field guide:
[`diagnostics.md`](diagnostics.md)):

```yaml
# syllabix.yaml
diagnostics:
  timestamps: true   # turn-*/turn.json sidecars under `directory`
  audio: true        # additionally capture/clean/utterance/tts.wav (implies timestamps)
  directory: target/turn-debug
```

Each sidecar carries `"timeline"` — monotonic milliseconds from the turn's
SpeechStart, captured at eleven stage boundaries: `speech_start`,
`speech_end`, `stt_queued`, `stt_done`, `llm_start`, `llm_first_token`,
`llm_last_token`, `tts_first_pcm`, `tts_last_pcm`, `playback_first` (first
speaker-callback samples), and `playback_done` (final audible drain).
Anchors a cancelled turn never reached render as `null`.

### Segments

| Segment | Formula | Reads as |
|---|---|---|
| `user_speech_ms` | speech_end − speech_start | How long the user spoke |
| `vad_queue_wait_ms` | stt_queued − speech_end | Utterance sat in queue |
| `stt_decode_ms` | stt_done − stt_queued | Whisper decode alone |
| `stt_total_ms` | stt_done − speech_end | Silence-end → transcript |
| `handoff_llm_ms` | llm_start − stt_done | Transcript → generation start |
| `llm_ttft_ms` | llm_first_token − llm_start | Time-to-first-token |
| `llm_stream_ms` | llm_last_token − llm_first_token | Generation duration |
| `tts_lead_ms` | tts_first_pcm − llm_first_token | First token → first PCM (sentence buffering visible) |
| `llm_end_to_first_pcm_ms` | tts_first_pcm − llm_last_token | Signed: negative ⇒ synthesis of a completed sentence overlapped generation; positive ⇒ TTS began after the LLM reply completed |
| `tts_synthesis_ms` | tts_last_pcm − tts_first_pcm | Synthesis throughput |
| `playback_handoff_ms` | playback_first − tts_first_pcm | PCM ready → device audible |
| **`audible_latency_ms`** | **playback_first − speech_end** | **Silence-end → first audio out of the speaker — the G4 budget metric** |
| `spoken_duration_ms` | playback_done − playback_first | Reply playback duration |
| `total_turn_ms` | playback_done − speech_end | Full round-trip |

The legacy TUI clocks are unchanged; `audible_latency_ms` will read higher
than the old TTFB because it now includes device handoff — that delta is the
instrumentation gap this row exists to expose.

Launch contract: the default is the best M4 16 GB combination for minimal
delight. The zero-config stack is whisper `small` + `lfm3-1.7b` + Pocket TTS.

Apple M4 / 16 GiB evidence in `docs/eval/runs/` still reports **`lfm2.5-2.6b`**
for the local LLM axis (first-token ~205–224 ms, ~56–64 tok/s, after-load RSS
~3.7 GB in those captures). Do not treat those rows as **`lfm3-1.7b`** numbers.
**`lfm3-1.7b` M4 TTFT, throughput, RSS, and profile-A timeline metrics are not
